comparison: Both strongly support the crystallographic structure determination of the four Ig-like domains (C5, C45-C66, C93). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of resolution, electron density, and structural features. Peer reviewers praised the structure as 'beautiful' and conducted with 'good level of rigor.' Minor difference: peer result includes C94 (structural comparison to homologs) while OpenEval addresses this separately in R17.

Perfect agreement on claims C67-C70, C100-C103 regarding cryo-EM and domain interaction studies. However, evaluations differ significantly: OpenEval rates these claims as UNCERTAIN due to conflicting evidence (low-resolution cryo-EM vs. negative binding data), while peer reviewers rate them SUPPORTED, explicitly commending authors for conducting additional experiments that 'fail to confirm their initial speculative model' and updating the manuscript accordingly.

Both support the systematic in vivo functional analysis of domain deletions (C73-C76, C78, C105-C107, C111-C112). OpenEval emphasizes the technical rigor of combining functional assays with western blots. Peer reviewers affirm 'in vivo experiments appear to be done well' with 'consistency in the findings.' Peer result also includes additional functional claims (C77, C79-C87, C114-C116) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Strong agreement on the decoupling of aggregation from biofilm/conjugation via binding cleft mutants (C88-C92, C118-C121). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from functional assays and EMSA data. Peer reviewers called this discovery 'exciting and well supported.' Peer result also includes C122-C124, C146 (conceptual conclusions about additional functions) which OpenEval addresses separately in R7.

Both address the major conceptual conclusion about PrgB having additional unknown functions beyond aggregation (C6, C122-C124, C146). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on experimental decoupling. Peer reviewers also support this, calling it 'exciting and well supported.' OpenEval treats this as a separate conceptual result while peer reviewers group it with the experimental evidence.

Both address protein stability and functional decoupling (C80, C86-C87, C112). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing western blot data ruling out degradation. Peer reviewers also support the functional work broadly. However, peer result groups these claims with the larger set of functional assays (R3), while OpenEval treats the stability-specific evidence as a distinct result.

Both support the structural reinterpretation of RGD motifs (C129-C132). OpenEval emphasizes the crystal structure showing RGD at buried interfaces, contradicting the integrin-binding hypothesis. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns and praised the structural work overall. Both treat this as well-supported by structural evidence, though OpenEval notes the structural defect mechanism (C131) is inferred rather than directly tested.

Major disagreement on claims C7, C117, C141-C145 regarding the rigid stalk model and distance requirements. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are hypotheses lacking direct experimental validation of stalk length, rigidity, or distance measurements. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the model without objection and describing it as 'impactful in the field.' This represents a significant difference in standards for mechanistic models.

Both address reinterpretation of literature data about linker regions (C134-C138). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are informed speculations about unfolded linkers and unreported phenotypes that remain untested. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the integration of 'new and previously published experimental data' without challenge. Difference reflects standards for speculative reinterpretations.

Both address reinterpretation of literature mutants based on the new structure (C125-C127). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are inferences not directly tested and alternative explanations cannot be excluded. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting the structural rationalization as part of the overall 'good level of rigor.' Difference in evaluation of indirect structural inferences.

Both support the negative findings and comparisons to homologs (C94-C99). OpenEval emphasizes structural comparison, literature citations, and appropriate caution about future ligands. Peer reviewers accepted these observations as part of the overall rigorous study. Strong agreement on these claims.

Both address synthesis of functional data regarding domain requirements (C104, C113-C116, C139-C140). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on systematic deletion analysis. Peer reviewers also support, noting 'convincing support for claims regarding overall function and importance of individual domains.' Strong agreement, though peer result groups these with broader reinterpretations.

Both address complementation validation and time-course stability data (C71-C72, C83-C85). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing western blots demonstrating normal production but time-dependent instability. Peer reviewers support the functional work broadly. OpenEval treats this as distinct methodological validation while peer reviewers group with overall functional assays.

Both address conjugation assay data showing correlation and partial rescue (C81-C82). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting this provides evidence for functional decoupling. Peer reviewers support the functional work broadly. OpenEval treats this as specific evidence for decoupling while peer reviewers include it in the general functional validation.

OpenEval addresses computational prediction and validation (C43-C44) as SUPPORTED, noting AlphaFold prediction was validated by crystal structure. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately discuss the computational prediction aspect.

OpenEval rates claims C108-C110 (COI-linker interaction hypothesis based on AlphaFold) as UNCERTAIN, noting this remains speculative without experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately address this mechanistic hypothesis.

OpenEval addresses technical protein production methods (C47-C49) as SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately discuss methodological details of protein production.

OpenEval addresses extensive background claims (C1-C42) as SUPPORTED, noting these represent established knowledge from prior literature providing context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately evaluate background/contextual claims.
